title: Prior-authorization request triage
problem: Incoming prior-authorization (PA) requests arrive as a mix of faxed forms, portal submissions, and attached clinical notes. Nurses manually read each one to identify the service requested and whether it meets policy criteria, creating a backlog and slow turnaround.
workflow: Utilization management intake queue; clinical review nurses.
data_availability: Historical PA requests with outcomes; medical policy criteria documents; structured request metadata.
stakeholders: UM nurses, medical directors, contracted providers, members awaiting care.
current_pain: Median turnaround of ~3 business days; nurses spend hours on routine, clearly-approvable requests instead of complex cases.

score.impact_rationale: PA is high-volume and directly delays member care; faster triage improves both cost and experience.
score.feasibility_rationale: Extracting requested service and criteria from semi-structured text is well within current NLP capability.
score.risk_rationale: Touches care decisions, so mis-routing carries clinical risk; mitigated by nurse confirmation on every case.
score.adoption_rationale: Nurses already triage; an assistive queue-sorter fits the existing workflow rather than replacing judgment.
score.strategic_value_rationale: PA modernization is a visible, board-level priority and a frequent source of provider abrasion.
score.roi_hypothesis: If 60% of routine requests auto-triage with nurse confirmation, median turnaround drops below one day and frees an estimated 15+ nurse-hours per week for complex cases.
score.ai_fit_reason: Pattern extraction and routing from messy text is a strong AI fit, with a nurse approving every authorization (decision support, not autonomy).

title: Claims-denial appeal letter drafting
problem: When a claim is denied, staff draft member- and provider-facing appeal-response letters from scratch, restating the denial reason, the relevant policy, and next steps. The letters are repetitive but must be accurate and compliant.
data_availability: Denial reason codes, policy references, and a library of approved letter templates and past letters.
stakeholders: Appeals analysts, compliance, members and providers receiving letters.
current_pain: Each letter takes 20-30 minutes to compose; volume spikes create backlogs and inconsistent tone.

score.impact_rationale: High letter volume with repetitive structure; drafting assistance saves substantial analyst time.
score.feasibility_rationale: Template-grounded generation from a denial code and policy reference is a mature LLM pattern.
score.risk_rationale: Regulated correspondence with required language; needs human review and template grounding to avoid inaccurate statements.
score.adoption_rationale: Analysts edit drafts they already would have written; low behavior change.
score.strategic_value_rationale: Improves consistency and timeliness of regulated member communications.
score.roi_hypothesis: A grounded first draft cuts letter time from ~25 to ~8 minutes; at current volume that is roughly one analyst-FTE of capacity returned.
score.ai_fit_reason: Drafting structured correspondence from known inputs with mandatory human review is a textbook generative-AI assist.

title: Member call summarization & next-best-action
problem: After each member service call, agents type a free-text wrap-up summary and choose follow-up actions. Summaries are inconsistent and time-consuming, and useful resolution patterns are not surfaced to the agent in the moment.
data_availability: Call transcripts (synthetic), disposition codes, knowledge-base articles.
current_pain: Average ~90 seconds of after-call work per call; inconsistent notes reduce downstream usefulness.

score.impact_rationale: Small per-call savings multiplied across very high call volume is material; better notes aid later interactions.
score.feasibility_rationale: Transcript summarization and suggested dispositions are among the most reliable LLM tasks today.
score.risk_rationale: Low-stakes internal notes; agent edits before saving, and no member-facing automated decision.
score.adoption_rationale: Removes a disliked manual step; agents are motivated to use it if accuracy is good.
score.strategic_value_rationale: Operational efficiency play; valuable but not differentiating on its own.
score.roi_hypothesis: Cutting after-call work by ~40 seconds per call returns meaningful agent capacity and shortens handle time at scale.
score.ai_fit_reason: Summarization with a human-edited, non-binding suggestion is a low-risk, high-confidence AI use.

title: Provider-directory data validation
problem: The provider directory drifts out of date as practices move, change hours, or stop accepting new patients. Inaccurate directories frustrate members and create regulatory exposure under directory-accuracy rules.
data_availability: Current directory records, outreach/verification logs, claims-derived activity signals.
stakeholders: Provider data team, network management, members searching for care, compliance.
current_pain: Manual outreach cannot keep pace; stale entries are found reactively via member complaints.

score.impact_rationale: Directory accuracy affects member access and carries direct regulatory penalties.
score.feasibility_rationale: Anomaly detection on records and activity signals is feasible but depends on data quality and labeling.
score.risk_rationale: Flags are reviewed before any record change; AI only prioritizes which entries to verify.
score.adoption_rationale: Requires the data team to trust and act on a prioritized worklist; needs a calibration period.
score.strategic_value_rationale: Compliance-driven hygiene; important but not a strategic differentiator.
score.roi_hypothesis: Proactively flagging the ~10% most-likely-stale records focuses outreach and reduces complaint-driven corrections.
score.ai_fit_reason: Prioritizing records for human verification via anomaly detection is an appropriate, bounded AI use.

title: Medical-policy Q&A assistant (retrieval-grounded)
problem: Clinical and operations staff frequently need to find the applicable rule inside a large, frequently-updated library of medical-policy bulletins and coverage guidelines. Searching by keyword is slow and often misses the governing document.
workflow: Policy reference during reviews and member inquiries.
data_availability: Full corpus of medical-policy documents and coverage guidelines (synthetic copies).
stakeholders: UM nurses, appeals analysts, member-service agents.
current_pain: Staff spend several minutes per lookup and sometimes cite outdated guidance.

score.impact_rationale: Saves time per lookup and improves citation accuracy, though each instance is small.
score.feasibility_rationale: Retrieval-augmented Q&A over a controlled document set is well-understood and grounded in source text.
score.risk_rationale: Answers cite source passages and staff verify; low risk when grounded and non-authoritative.
score.adoption_rationale: Natural-language search is intuitive and clearly better than keyword search for this corpus.
score.strategic_value_rationale: Enabling capability that supports several downstream workflows.
score.roi_hypothesis: Reducing policy-lookup time and mis-citations improves review accuracy and shaves minutes from many daily tasks.
score.ai_fit_reason: Grounded retrieval over a curated corpus, with citations and human verification, is a reliable AI fit.

title: Fraud, waste & abuse anomaly detection
problem: Investigators review claims for fraud, waste, and abuse largely from rules and tips. Novel billing patterns slip through fixed rules, and analysts cannot manually scan the full claims stream for outliers.
data_availability: Historical claims with confirmed FWA labels (synthetic), provider and procedure reference data.
current_pain: Rule-based detection is reactive and misses emerging schemes; analysts are capacity-constrained.

score.impact_rationale: FWA recovery and avoidance is high-dollar; surfacing novel patterns has large financial upside.
score.feasibility_rationale: Anomaly detection is feasible but label scarcity and class imbalance make precision hard to guarantee.
score.risk_rationale: False positives can unfairly burden providers; every lead must be investigated by a human before action.
score.adoption_rationale: Investigators must trust model-generated leads; requires explainable scoring and a feedback loop.
score.strategic_value_rationale: Directly supports payment-integrity goals and complements existing rules.
score.roi_hypothesis: Even a modest lift in detected, recoverable FWA over rules-only baseline materially exceeds the build cost.
score.ai_fit_reason: Outlier detection that generates human-investigated leads (not automated adverse action) is a well-scoped AI use.

title: Member dissatisfaction & churn risk prediction
problem: Retention efforts are largely reactive. The plan wants to identify members at elevated risk of dissatisfaction or non-renewal early enough to intervene with outreach.
data_availability: Interaction history, complaint and grievance signals, utilization and survey data (all synthetic).
current_pain: Outreach is untargeted; at-risk members are often identified only after they disenroll.

score.impact_rationale: Retention upside is real but diffuse and hard to attribute to any single intervention.
score.feasibility_rationale: Predictive modeling is feasible but signal quality and intervention linkage are uncertain.
score.risk_rationale: Outreach is benign; main concern is fairness/bias in who gets targeted, which is auditable.
score.adoption_rationale: Requires retention staff to operationalize scores into outreach plays.
score.strategic_value_rationale: Supports retention goals but competes with simpler segmentation approaches.
score.roi_hypothesis: If targeted outreach lifts retention of flagged members even slightly, retained premium outweighs program cost.
score.ai_fit_reason: Risk scoring to prioritize benign human outreach is an acceptable AI use, provided targeting is monitored for bias.

title: Autonomous medical-necessity denial decisions
problem: A proposal to have the model make final medical-necessity denial determinations end-to-end, issuing denials automatically when criteria appear unmet, to eliminate the clinical-review bottleneck entirely.
data_availability: Historical determinations and clinical criteria; outcome data.
stakeholders: Medical directors, UM nurses, members, regulators.
current_pain: Clinical review is a bottleneck; leadership wants the queue gone, not just faster.

score.impact_rationale: Would remove a real bottleneck if it were permissible — but the impact is moot given the fit problem.
score.feasibility_rationale: Reliable autonomous medical-necessity judgment across edge cases is not achievable at the required accuracy.
score.risk_rationale: Automated adverse coverage decisions create severe member-harm, regulatory, and legal exposure.
score.adoption_rationale: Clinicians and regulators will not accept AI issuing denials without licensed human judgment.
score.strategic_value_rationale: Pursuing this would damage trust and invite scrutiny, outweighing any efficiency gain.
score.roi_hypothesis: No defensible ROI: regulatory, legal, and reputational liability dominates any labor savings.
score.ai_fit_reason: NOT A FIT. A final adverse coverage determination requires licensed clinical judgment and member due-process/appeal rights. AI may support the review, but it must not autonomously deny care. Reframe as decision support (see prior-auth-triage).

title: Monthly premium billing reconciliation
problem: A request to use an LLM to recompute and reconcile monthly premium invoices against the general ledger, matching payments to member accounts and flagging discrepancies.
data_availability: Structured billing records, payment files, and ledger entries.
current_pain: Month-end reconciliation is tedious and the team wants to automate it.

score.impact_rationale: Automating reconciliation is valuable, but the value is realized by deterministic tooling, not AI.
score.feasibility_rationale: An LLM introduces nondeterminism and arithmetic errors into a problem that has an exact, rule-based solution.
score.risk_rationale: Financial figures demand exactness and auditability; probabilistic output is the wrong instrument and harder to audit.
score.adoption_rationale: Finance and audit will rightly distrust non-reproducible figures.
score.strategic_value_rationale: No strategic upside to applying AI where a deterministic system is cheaper and more correct.
score.roi_hypothesis: Negative versus the right baseline: a SQL/rules reconciliation job is cheaper, exact, and auditable.
score.ai_fit_reason: NOT A FIT. This is deterministic arithmetic and ledger matching. A rules engine or SQL job is exact, reproducible, auditable, and cheaper. An LLM adds error and nondeterminism to a solved problem.

title: Real-time eligibility lookup at point of service
problem: A request to build an AI model that answers whether a member is currently eligible for coverage when a provider checks at the point of service.
data_availability: Authoritative enrollment database with current eligibility status accessible via API.
current_pain: Providers want a fast, reliable eligibility answer at the point of service.

score.impact_rationale: Fast eligibility answers matter, but the need is met by a direct system lookup, not inference.
score.feasibility_rationale: Framing a deterministic database lookup as an ML problem is unnecessary and would be less accurate.
score.risk_rationale: A predicted eligibility status could be wrong where the source of truth is exact and authoritative.
score.adoption_rationale: Providers need the authoritative answer, not a probabilistic estimate of it.
score.strategic_value_rationale: No strategic value in modeling a value that can simply be queried.
score.roi_hypothesis: A straightforward API integration to the enrollment system delivers this at lower cost and higher accuracy.
score.ai_fit_reason: NOT A FIT. Eligibility is an authoritative lookup against the enrollment system of record. This is integration/engineering work (an API call), not a prediction problem; AI would only add error.
